thread:
olivia: heads up — BERTScore numbers look way worse for the int8 quantized model vs fp16 on the squad-ish eval set, but exact_match/bleu are fine. unsure if this is real quality drop or metric plumbing.
raj: could be tokenization differences. did we pin the tokenizer for the quant build? small detokenization/norm changes wreck bertscore since it compares text embeddings.
miguel: our runner image used transformers 4.31 in master, but the quant infra image still had 4.28. prob mismatch.
olivia: good call. here's a quick diff from the failing run:
```
# bertscore call in eval runner
score = bert_score.compute(preds=outputs, refs=gold, lang='en', rescale_with_baseline=True)
# tokenizer setup earlier
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name_or_path, use_fast=True)
```
sara: also check whether we feed normalized text to BERTScore (lowercasing, punctuation strip). we sometimes apply normalize_answer() for exact_match but not for bertscore.
olivia: aha — the eval harness currently does: exact_match_normalize -> yes, bertscore uses raw detok from model. so mismatch.
raj: two orthogonal issues then: tokenizer lib mismatch between images, and inconsistent normalization. both explain the gap.
miguel: CI note: the quant runner also prunes some special tokens differently due to fast tokenizer bug in 4.28. that will change embedding inputs.
eval-ci-bot: CI #345: bertscore_mean dropped from 0.91 -> 0.73 after quantization. threshold 0.85 => alert triggered. See logs: link-to-ci/345
sara: proposed fixes: (1) pin transformers in the quant image to the same version as main; (2) unify normalization pipeline: create eval.normalize_text() used by all metrics; (3) rerun with bertscore params idf=False, rescale_with_baseline=False for stability check.
olivia: +1. also can we try computing bertscore on subword-token-aligned detokenization to rule out detok differences? basically feed the same token->text path for both models.
raj: small patch for normalize_text I sketched:
```
def normalize_text(s: str) -> str:
    s = s.lower().strip()
    s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s)
    s = s.replace("’", "'")
    s = s.translate(str.maketrans('', '', string.punctuation))
    return s
```
miguel: careful removing punctuation: that will spike BLEU/ROUGE behavior. maybe parametrize: normalize_text(s, for_exact_match=True/False) or metric-specific normalizers in a single util module.
sara: agreed. add a small test matrix in CI: run metric set = [exact_match(normalize=True), bertscore(normalize=False), bertscore(normalize=True)] and diff. flag any >X delta.
olivia: also we should audit pass@k implementation: I found runner counting duplicates across seeds which inflates pass@k when deduping is off. separate PR incoming.
raj: pass@k note — ensure sampling randomness seed is logged. current runner reuses the same candidate pool uid across shards, causing double-counting.
eval-ci-bot: ticket created: EVAL-212 "bertokenizer+quant mismatch causing metric regression" (priority P2).
miguel: timeline: I can ship a new quant image pinned to transformers 4.31 and add a smoke job that runs tokenizer parity in 2 hours.
sara: I'll add the normalize_text util and CI matrix today, plus a tiny dashboard alert on the metrics dashboard that shows tokenizer_version used per run. helps debugging next time.
olivia: sounds good. after fixes, rerun quant experiments and attach paired t-test for bertscore differences. if still significant, then we have real quality regression to troubleshoot in quant kernels.
raj: we might also embed a tiny regression harness that runs on a canonical seed set (100 examples) to check calibration and BERTScore drift before full-run costs.
olivia: yep. thanks team. tagging follow-ups: @miguel will update images, @sara will patch harness + dashboard, @raj will patch pass@k dedup fix and add tests. i'll re-run experiments once infra is stable. :thumbsup:
